title: Anti-spin Laue groups: classification of anti-altermagnets and their representative minimal models
authors: Colin Lange, Rodrigo Jaeschke-Ubiergo, Alexander Mook, Jairo Sinova
abstract: Anti-altermagnets exhibit odd-parity nonrelativistic spin splitting, yet unlike even-parity altermagnets, their momentum-space symmetries lack a reduced classification analogous to spin Laue groups. Here, we introduce anti-spin Laue groups, organized into three distinct classes, and identify 21 groups describing the odd-parity partial wave character of this unconventional class. Together with the 10 spin Laue groups of altermagnets, they complete the classification of nonrelativistic unconventional magnets with collinear momentum-space spin polarization. Anti-spin Laue groups also provide a many-to-one reduction of spin space (point) groups by retaining only their action on the collinear momentum-space spin polarization, thereby directly encoding the symmetry-enforced nodal spin-splitting character. Based on this we develop a systematic model-construction algorithm yielding minimal, material-oriented four-band models. This framework places odd- and even-parity unconventional magnets on equal footing within a unified momentum-space symmetry description.
summary: This paper introduces the concept of anti-spin Laue groups to systematically classify anti-altermagnets, which exhibit unique odd-parity spin splitting. By developing this classification, the authors create a unified theoretical framework that allows for the construction of minimal, material-oriented four-band models for unconventional magnets. This advances the understanding of how magnetic symmetry dictates electronic band structure in condensed matter systems.
main_problem: To classify and develop minimal theoretical models for anti-altermagnets, which exhibit odd-parity nonrelativistic spin splitting and lack a simple symmetry classification analogous to existing spin Laue groups.
main_result: The authors introduce anti-spin Laue groups, classifying 21 distinct groups that, together with spin Laue groups, provide a complete symmetry description for unconventional magnets with collinear momentum-space spin polarization.
method: The classification is achieved by projecting the full spin group onto the action on the out-of-plane spin polarization component, leading to a systematic model-construction algorithm for minimal four-band Hamiltonians.
model_or_system: The focus is on anti-altermagnets, which are coplanar magnets characterized by odd-parity nonrelativistic spin splitting. The theoretical framework unifies the symmetry description for both odd- and even-parity unconventional magnets.
key_observables: The perpendicular spin polarization component, $S_{\perp}(k)$, and the resulting symmetry-enforced nodal spin-splitting character.
important_parameters: Odd-parity spin splitting, collinear momentum-space spin polarization, and the structure of the anti-spin Laue groups ($	ext{R}_{	ext{Is}}, 	ext{R}_{	ext{IIs}}, 	ext{R}_{	ext{IIIs}}$).
main_assumptions: The construction retains only the action of the spin symmetry on the collinear momentum-space spin polarization, and an effective 'anti-inversion' symmetry must be added for anti-spin Laue groups.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the relationship between different real-space lattice models belonging to the same anti-spin Laue group, showing common nodal structures in momentum space, and visualizing the perpendicular spin polarization $S_{\perp}$ and nodal planes for various crystal systems.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the need for anti-spin Laue groups due to the unique symmetry of anti-altermagnets. It then details the construction of these groups, provides a comprehensive classification (21 groups), and concludes by presenting a systematic algorithm to build minimal, material-oriented four-band models.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, symmetry-enforced framework for understanding magnetic electronic structure, which is crucial for designing novel topological or correlated electronic materials relevant to quantum phenomena.
